title_en: Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company Limited v. Xuchang Ruishi Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of invention patent
ruling_gist_en: In cases of patent infringement disputes, in order to correctly understand the claims and accurately determine the scope of protection of the patent claims, the technical features in the claims shall be reasonably interpreted in light of the patent specification, drawings, and patent prosecution documents. Where a person of ordinary skill in the art can reasonably ascertain substitutable portions of the technical features of the claims without the need for inventive effort, and adopts a change in part of the structure to achieve the same function and effect, such shall be deemed to have equivalent features. If the technical composition of the accused infringing product is identical or equivalent to the technical features recorded in the patent claims in terms of means, function, effect, purpose, manner, etc., it shall be determined as constituting infringement.

full_text_en:
Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company Limited v. Xuchang Ruishi Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of invention patent

【Ruling Summary】

In disputes over infringement of patent rights, to correctly understand the claims and accurately determine the scope of protection of the patent claims, the technical features in the claims shall be reasonably interpreted in light of the patent specification, drawings, and patent examination documents. Where a person of ordinary skill in the art, without the need for creative labor, can reasonably ascertain substitutable parts of the technical features in the claims, and adopts changes to part of the structure to achieve the same function and effect, such shall be deemed to have equivalent features. Where the technical composition of the accused infringing product is identical or equivalent to the technical features recorded in the patent claims in terms of means of implementation, function, effect, purpose, mode, etc., it shall be determined that infringement has been constituted.

Plaintiff: Tsinghua University, domiciled at: Haidian District, Beijing, Tsinghua Yuan.
Legal representative: Qiu Yong, President of the University.

Plaintiff: Nuctech Company Limited, domiciled at: Haidian District, Beijing, Shuangqing Road.
Legal representative: Chen Zhiqiang, Chairman of the Board.

Defendant: Xuchang Ruishi Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at: the west side of the intersection of Zhouzhai Road and Shangji Street, core area of Zhongyuan Electric Valley, Xuchang City.
Legal representative: Wang Mancang, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiffs, Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as "Nuctech"), filed a lawsuit with the Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province against the defendant, Xuchang Ruishi Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Xuchang Ruishi"), for disputes over infringement of invention patent rights.

The plaintiffs, Tsinghua University and Nuctech, alleged: Nuctech is the patentee of Invention Patent No. ZL200710304704.8. Tsinghua University, authorized by Nuctech, has the right to jointly claim rights against any infringement of the patent in this case. The invention name of the patent in this case is "A Dual-View Scanning Device Arm Structure," which was granted the patent right by the State Intellectual Property Office on December 28, 2011, effective from December 28, 2007, to December 27, 2027. According to the copy of the patent register, the patent in this case is currently in force. The patent in this case includes nine claims. Claims 1-9 relate to a dual-view scanning device arm structure. The defendant, Xuchang Ruishi, was established in 2014 and is an enterprise specialized in the production and sale of X-ray safety inspection equipment and metal detection equipment, competing with the plaintiffs in the same industry. After analysis and comparison, the dual-view scanning device arm structure included in the container/vehicle inspection system manufactured, offered for sale, and sold by Xuchang Ruishi falls within the scope of protection of Claims 1-9 of the patent in this case. According to Article 11, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, after the grant of an invention or utility model patent, except as otherwise provided by law, no entity or individual may, without the permission of the patentee, exploit the patent, that is, may not, for production or business purposes, manufacture, use, offer to sell, sell, or import the patented product. In this case, without the permission of the plaintiffs, Xuchang Ruishi engaged in the acts of manufacturing, offering for sale, and selling the "dual-view scanning device arm structure" that falls within the scope of protection of the patent in this case. The above acts all violate Article 11, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, infringing the lawful rights and interests of the plaintiffs, and shall bear corresponding legal liability. The plaintiffs requested the court to order: 1. Xuchang Ruishi to cease manufacturing, offering for sale, and selling the accused infringing product; 2. Xuchang Ruishi to compensate Tsinghua University and Nuctech for economic losses and reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringement, totaling RMB 1,100,000; 3. Xuchang Ruishi to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The defendant, Xuchang Ruishi, argued: 1. The plaintiff Tsinghua University is neither the inventor nor the patentee of the patent in suit and does not have standing to sue as a plaintiff in this case; 2. The products of Xuchang Ruishi are only prototypes for experimental research and development, not finished products, and its conduct does not constitute manufacturing under patent law, let alone offering for sale or selling; 3. The products of Xuchang Ruishi do not contain technical features identical to all the technical features recorded in the claims of the patent in suit, as there is (1) no collimator column; (2) the detectors are not uniformly installed; (3) the mounting brackets for the detectors are not adjustable, and thus do not constitute infringement of the patent in suit; 4. The plaintiffs' claim for compensation of economic losses and reasonable expenses of RMB 1,100,000 lacks factual and legal basis and should be dismissed. The defendant requested the court to reject all claims of Tsinghua University and Nuctech.

The Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province found at first instance:

On December 28, 2007, the plaintiff Nuctech filed an application with the State Intellectual Property Office for an invention patent titled "A Dual-View Scanning Device Arm Structure," which was granted on December 28, 2011, with patent number ZL200710304704.8. The claims of the patent are as follows: 1. A dual-view scanning device arm structure, comprising the following components: a collimator column, a main beam, a horizontal detection arm, a vertical detection arm, a vertical detection arm column, and a collimator, characterized in that the collimator column and the vertical detection arm column are connected to the main beam, serving as the frame of the scanning device arm structure, providing support and adjustment mechanisms for the collimator, the horizontal detection arm, and the vertical detection arm; on the horizontal detection arm, within the areas of two ray planes at a certain angle to which X-rays are directed, radiation detectors are uniformly installed, and the mounting brackets of the radiation detectors are adjustable to ensure that the detection surfaces of the radiation detectors face the X-rays directly, thereby making the detected X-ray signal the strongest; 2. The scanning device arm structure according to claim 1, characterized in that the frame of the scanning device arm structure is an integral gantry structure; 3. The scanning device arm structure according to claim 1, characterized in that there is also a mounting bracket on the main beam for installing a detector cooling system that cools all radiation detectors; 4. The scanning device arm structure according to claim 1, characterized in that on the vertical detection arm, within the areas of two ray planes at a certain angle to which X-rays are directed, radiation detectors are uniformly installed; the vertical detection arm is also provided with an adjustment device for adjusting the vertical detection arm to ensure that the detection surfaces of the radiation detectors face the X-rays directly, making the detected X-ray signal the strongest; 5. The scanning device arm structure according to claim 4, characterized in that the radiation detector array installed on the vertical detection arm is higher than the radiation detectors installed on the horizontal detection arm, so that X-rays on the diagonal of the detection plane can also be detected; 6. The arm structure according to claim 1, wherein the collimator is connected to the collimator column via a lower support and an adjustment support, and adjusting the adjustment bolts can cause the collimator to translate and rotate; 7. The arm structure according to claim 1, wherein the horizontal detection arm is connected to the main beam via a mounting support; 8. The arm structure according to claim 7, characterized in that it further comprises: a horizontal detection arm adjustment device, having lateral adjustment bolts and longitudinal adjustment bolts; adjusting the lateral adjustment bolts can cause the horizontal detection arm to translate and swing; adjusting the longitudinal adjustment bolts can adjust the relative position of the horizontal detection arm and the vertical detection arm; 9. The arm structure according to claim 1, characterized in that the vertical detection arm includes a left vertical detection arm and a right vertical detection arm, connected to the vertical detection column via a lower support and an adjustment support, and by adjusting the adjustment bolts, the left vertical detection arm and the right vertical detection arm can be translated and rotated. During the proceedings, the plaintiffs clarified that the scope of patent protection they assert in this case covers claims 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the patent in suit.

In November 2016, the plaintiffs discovered that the defendant Xuchang Ruishi was engaged in the production and manufacturing of container vehicle inspection equipment, and believed that the product might use relevant patented technology of the plaintiffs, and subsequently initiated an investigation. Notarized Document (2016) Jing Hai Cheng Nei Min Zheng Zi No. 16027 states: The "Environmental Impact Report for the Production, Sale, and Use Project of Container Vehicle Inspection Equipment by Xuchang Ruishi Company" compiled in August 2016 published on the Henan Provincial Environmental Protection Department website, which shows the basic structure and relevant technical data of the container inspection equipment that Xuchang Ruishi plans to produce. Notarized Document (2016) Jing Hai Cheng Nei Min Zheng Zi No. 16031 states: On the website of Shanghai Ruishi Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai Ruishi), the Ruishi quarterly product information section publicly displays and promotes photos of the container/vehicle inspection system model CBS62-405, along with text descriptions of the product's system advantages, technical indicators, etc. There are descriptions of technical features such as "dual-view imaging technology, multi-row sealed array pencil detectors." The product model is consistent with the product located at the production site of Xuchang Ruishi that was subject to evidence preservation and on-site inspection by the court. Xuchang Ruishi participated in the customs 2016 container and vehicle inspection system (re-bidding) in December 2016, bidding for Package 02 "Multi-functional large container/vehicle inspection system" and Package 05 "Through-type rapid inspection system."

On January 14, 2017, the plaintiffs issued a "Certificate of Intellectual Property License," stating that Nuctech licenses Tsinghua University to use multiple patents, computer software copyrights, and technical secrets, including the patent in suit, in research and commercial development, and authorizes Tsinghua University to jointly claim rights against any alleged infringer of the intellectual property rights, including but not limited to filing lawsuits with the People's Court and filing complaints with the competent intellectual property authorities.

The plaintiffs paid attorney fees of RMB 400,000 for investigating the patent infringement facts and litigation. During the proceedings, the two plaintiffs submitted invoices for attorney fees but did not provide corresponding legal service contracts.

During the proceedings, upon the plaintiffs' application, the court lawfully made a ruling on evidence preservation and went to Xuchang Ruishi's production site in Luohe on January 23, 2017, for evidence preservation. Because the Chinese New Year was approaching, the factory of Xuchang Ruishi was closed, and employees were on leave, so the court could not enter the factory for preservation. After contacting the legal representative of Xuchang Ruishi by phone, the court lawfully affixed seals to the various doors of the factory, took photos and videos of the interior through the door cracks, and scheduled an on-site inspection and comparison on February 6, 2017, which was the first working day after the holiday. On February 6, 2017, the court organized the plaintiffs and defendant to conduct an on-site inspection and comparison of the container/vehicle inspection system model CBS62-405 at Xuchang Ruishi's factory, and took photos and videos of the product.

The Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province held at first instance:

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of Claims 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the patent in suit; 2. Whether the acts of the defendant Xuchang Ruishi constitute patent infringement such as manufacturing, selling, and offering for sale under patent law; 3. Whether the plaintiffs' claim for compensation of losses and reasonable expenses of RMB 1,100,000 should be supported.

Regarding the issue of Tsinghua University's standing as a plaintiff: Although the patentee of the patent in suit is Nuctech, Nuctech issued the "Certificate of Intellectual Property License," authorizing Tsinghua University to use the patent in suit and to jointly claim rights against any alleged infringer with Nuctech. Therefore, Tsinghua University, as a co-plaintiff in this case, complies with relevant legal provisions.

Regarding the first issue in dispute, i.e., whether the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of Claims 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the patent in suit. Article 59, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China provides: The scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of the claims; the description and drawings may be used to interpret the claims. Article 17 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases provides: The "scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of the claims; the description and drawings may be used to interpret the claims" as referred to in Article 59, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law means that the scope of protection of the patent shall be determined by the scope defined by all the technical features recorded in the claims, including the scope defined by features equivalent to those technical features. Equivalent features refer to features that achieve substantially the same function, produce substantially the same effect, by substantially the same means as the recorded technical features, and that a person of ordinary skill in the art, without the need for creative labor, can conceive at the time of the alleged infringing act occurs. Regarding the comparison between the accused product and the scope of protection of the patent in suit, the main points of dispute between the parties focus on three technical features in Claim 1, namely: whether the accused infringing product has a collimator column; whether the detectors of the accused infringing product are uniformly installed; and whether the mounting brackets are adjustable. The court held: From the description of the technical feature "collimator column" in Claim 1, in terms of positional relationship, the collimator column and the vertical detection arm column are connected to the main beam, serving as a frame; in terms of function and effect, the collimator column, as part of the frame, provides support for the collimator. Through on-site inspection, the accelerator compartment of the accused infringing product, together with its upper bracket, forms a support body, which is connected to the upper main beam, similarly serving as part of the overall frame to provide support for the collimator, and such support structure can be conceived by a person of ordinary skill in the art without the need for creative labor. Therefore, such support structure of the accused infringing product can be recognized as an equivalent feature of the collimator column in the patent in suit.

Regarding the issue of whether the detectors of the accused infringing product are uniformly installed: From the description of the technical feature "uniformly installed detectors" in Claim 1, uniform installation does not mean that the horizontal spacing between each detector on the horizontal detection arm is equal. Drawing 1 of the patent in suit also clearly shows that the "within the ray plane area, uniformly installed radiation detectors" described in the patent in suit means that the detectors are closely arranged within the fan beam plane. Within the ray plane area, viewed from the radiation source toward the detectors, the detectors are closely and uniformly arranged, aiming not to miss any rays, thereby achieving the most basic requirement of security inspection. The defendant Xuchang Ruishi also clearly confirmed during the trial that its product also needs to achieve the technical effect of not missing rays; the detectors are not randomly arranged but are scientifically calculated based on different angles, and the rays are continuous, capable of achieving the technical effect of not missing rays. Therefore, it can be determined that the radiation detectors of the accused infringing product are also uniformly installed within the ray plane area, which is identical to the technical feature of the patent in suit.

Regarding the issue of whether the mounting brackets of the accused infringing product are adjustable: From the description of the technical feature "mounting bracket" in Claim 1 of the patent in suit, the mounting bracket is used to adjust the relative position of the radiation detector and the X-ray fan beam plane, and the radiation detector is located in the horizontal detection arm, which is connected to the main beam via the mounting support. Therefore, the language of the claim also indicates that the horizontal detection arm and the mounting support together constitute the mounting bracket for the detector. During the on-site inspection, the product of the defendant Xuchang Ruishi could adjust the mounting bracket of the radiation detector by changing the position of the bolts in the mounting slots of the mounting support, to make the detected X-ray signal the strongest. The description of Claim 1 of the patent in suit clearly states: "the mounting brackets of the radiation detectors are adjustable to ensure that the detection surfaces of the radiation detectors face the X-rays directly," meaning that the "adjustable mounting brackets of the radiation detectors" in Claim 1 refers to the adjustability of the orientation of the mounting brackets relative to the X-ray fan beam plane, not, as Xuchang Ruishi argued, whether the mounting brackets of the radiation detectors can be adjusted relative to the horizontal detection arm. In summary, all technical features of the accused infringing product and Claim 1 of the patent in suit are identical or equivalent, thus the accused product falls within the scope of protection of Claim 1 of the patent in suit.

Regarding Claims 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8, the court held: The gantry structure does not require left-right symmetry; it is sufficient that the product frame can form a stable gantry structure with left and right supports and a top beam. The overall structure of the accused infringing product presents a gantry structure, thus it falls within the scope of protection of dependent Claim 2 of the patent in suit. Similar to the horizontal detection arm, the detectors on the vertical detection arm are also uniformly distributed within the ray plane area and have an adjustment device to adjust their position, therefore the accused product falls within the scope of protection of Claim 4. The defendant Xuchang Ruishi did not dispute the fact that the uppermost part of the radiation detector on the vertical detection arm of the accused infringing product is higher than the radiation detector installed on the horizontal detection arm. Therefore, the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of dependent Claim 5 of the patent in suit. From the on-site inspection, it can be seen that the collimator of Xuchang Ruishi's product is connected to the collimator column via a lower support and an adjustment support. The lower part of the collimator has translation adjustment bolts and adjustment bolt supports, as well as rotation adjustment bolts and adjustment bolt supports; the upper part of the collimator has translation adjustment bolts and adjustment bolt supports, indicating that the collimator of the accused infringing product can be translated and rotated by adjusting the adjustment bolts. Thus, the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of dependent Claim 6 of the patent in suit. The horizontal detection arm of Xuchang Ruishi's product is connected to the main beam via a mounting support, which includes a protruding part welded onto the horizontal detection arm. Therefore, the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of dependent Claim 7 of the patent in suit. The horizontal detection arm adjustment device of the accused infringing product includes adjustment bolts, which achieve movement of the horizontal detection arm through displacement in the horizontal and vertical mounting slots. Therefore, the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of dependent Claim 8 of the patent in suit.

In summary, the CBS62-405 container/vehicle inspection system produced by the defendant Xuchang Ruishi falls within the scope of protection of Claims 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the invention patent No. ZL200710304704.8, titled "A Dual-View Scanning Device Arm Structure," and constitutes infringement.

Regarding the second issue in dispute, i.e., whether the actions of the defendant Xuchang Ruishi Company constitute acts of manufacture, sale, and offer for sale under patent law. The court found that: According to evidence obtained from the on-site inspection, Xuchang Ruishi Company manufactured at least one set of the CBS62-405 container/vehicle inspection system product, and this CBS62-405 product fully fell within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit. The "Environmental Impact Report for the Production, Sale, and Use Project of Container Vehicle Inspection Equipment by Xuchang Ruishi Company" published on the website of the Henan Provincial Department of Environmental Protection showed that Xuchang Ruishi Company had undergone the relevant administrative approval procedures for producing the accused infringing product. Therefore, it could be determined that Xuchang Ruishi Company's actions constituted manufacturing for the purpose of production and operation. Xuchang Ruishi Company, without permission, manufactured a patented product for the purpose of production and operation, constituting infringement, and should bear the legal liability of ceasing infringement and compensating for losses. The plaintiff in this case failed to provide evidence that Xuchang Ruishi Company had sold the accused infringing product. Therefore, the court did not support the plaintiff's claim requesting that Xuchang Ruishi Company bear the infringement liability for ceasing sales. As for the evidence submitted by the plaintiff showing that Shanghai Ruishi Company displayed similar products and that Xuchang Ruishi Company participated in bidding in this case, given that Xuchang Ruishi Company is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Shanghai Ruishi Company with the same legal representative, the model and related functional descriptions and technical specifications of the product displayed by Shanghai Ruishi Company were consistent with the accused infringing product manufactured by Xuchang Ruishi Company. Xuchang Ruishi Company also did not provide evidence showing that Shanghai Ruishi Company had other production capabilities or facilities for the displayed product. Therefore, it could be determined that Xuchang Ruishi Company had engaged in acts of offering for sale of the accused infringing product. Accordingly, the court supported the plaintiff's claim requesting that Xuchang Ruishi Company bear the infringement liability for ceasing the offer for sale.

Regarding the third issue in dispute, i.e., whether the plaintiff's claim for compensation for losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 1,100,000 should be supported. The court found that: According to the provisions of Article 65 of the Patent Law, the amount of damages for patent infringement shall be determined based on the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to the infringement. If the actual losses are difficult to determine, the amount may be determined based on the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement. If the losses of the right holder or the profits gained by the infringer are difficult to determine, the amount shall be determined reasonably by reference to a multiple of the patent licensing fee. The amount of damages shall also include the reasonable expenses incurred by the right holder in stopping the infringement. If the losses of the right holder, the profits gained by the infringer, and the patent licensing fee are all difficult to determine, the people's court may determine damages ranging from RMB 10,000 to RMB 1,000,000 based on factors such as the type of patent, the nature and circumstances of the infringement. In this case, the losses suffered by the plaintiff due to the infringement or the profits gained by the defendant Xuchang Ruishi Company from the infringement could not be verified. Considering that the patent-in-suit is an invention patent, that the value of such complete sets of equipment is relatively high, that the defendant is a manufacturing enterprise, and the reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiff in investigating and stopping the infringement, the court determines the amount of damages in this case to be RMB 500,000.

Accordingly, the Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province, pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 11, Paragraph 1 of Article 59, and Article 65 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 17 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases, and Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on August 10, 2017:

1. The defendant Xuchang Ruishi Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease the acts of manufacturing and offering for sale products that infringe the invention patent right of the plaintiffs, Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company Limited, for Patent No. ZL200710304704.8 titled "A Double-View Scanning Apparatus Arm Structure";

2. The defendant Xuchang Ruishi Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the plaintiffs Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company Limited for economic losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 500,000;

3. The other claims of the plaintiffs Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company Limited are dismissed.

Xuchang Ruishi Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Henan High People's Court.

Xuchang Ruishi Company appealed, arguing: First, the first-instance court erred in finding that Tsinghua University was a proper plaintiff in this case and in ordering Xuchang Ruishi Company to cease infringing Tsinghua University's invention patent and compensate Tsinghua University for economic losses. (a) Although the "Intellectual Property License and Use Certificate" issued by Nuctech Company stated that Tsinghua University had the right to file a lawsuit with Nuctech Company against suspected infringers in the people's court, Tsinghua University did not have a direct interest in this case. Tsinghua University, as a public welfare educational institution, does not engage in profit-making production and operation activities. Tsinghua University's use of the patent-in-suit is only for scientific research and development, and it would not suffer operational profit losses due to the alleged infringement. Therefore, Tsinghua University has no direct interest in the other parties in this case and is not a proper plaintiff. Tsinghua University's claim for damages from Xuchang Ruishi Company lacks legal basis. The first-instance court's listing of Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company as co-plaintiffs and ordering Xuchang Ruishi Company to cease infringing Tsinghua University's patent right and compensate for losses was insufficiently evidenced and should be corrected.

Second, the first-instance judgment erred in finding that the accused infringing product, CBS62-405 container/vehicle inspection system, fell within the protection scope of claims 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the patent-in-suit:

(a) The "accelerator chamber and its upper support" in the accused infringing product and the "collimator column" in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit are not equivalent features. First, they employ completely different means. The collimator column in the patent-in-suit is a column, while the accelerator chamber in the accused infringing product is a box structure. The structures of a "box" and a "column" are different. Therefore, the first-instance judgment's generic identification of the "accelerator chamber and its upper box" as an upper-level concept (i.e., a support body) in relation to the "collimator column" in claim 1, and thus as substantially the same means, constitutes an error in fact finding. Second, their functions and effects are different. The accelerator chamber in the accused infringing product is a box that can protect the collimator and achieve the effect of preventing radiation leakage. In contrast, the collimator column in the patent-in-suit is merely a column capable of providing support and does not have the function or effect of an accelerator chamber. Additionally, the design motivation for the two structures is entirely different. The collimator column in the patent-in-suit pursues a simple outer frame structure, whereas the accelerator chamber with an internal collimator in the accused infringing product is designed from the perspective of protecting the collimator and ensuring safety of use, integrating the radiation source emitting part. This change from a column to a box is not a feature that a person of ordinary skill in the art would conceive without creative effort. Therefore, the "accelerator chamber and its upper support" in the accused infringing product and the "collimator column" in claim 1 are not equivalent features.

(b) The accused infringing product does not possess the technical feature "on the transverse detection arm (103), within the two angled ray surface areas where X-rays are emitted, radiation detectors are uniformly installed," and thus does not fall within the protection scope of claim 1. The explanation in the first-instance judgment introduces content that does not exist in the claims or specification of the patent-in-suit, constituting errors in fact finding and legal application. Furthermore, the first-instance court did not inspect the specific installation spacing of the detectors on the transverse detection arm of the accused infringing product. In fact, the detectors on the transverse detection arm of the accused infringing product are not uniformly installed, nor is there a "close and uniform arrangement of detectors." Therefore, the first-instance judgment's conclusion that "the radiation detectors of the accused infringing product are also uniformly installed within the ray surface area" constitutes an error in fact finding.

(c) The accused infringing product does not possess the technical feature "the installation support for the radiation detectors is adjustable to ensure that the detection surfaces of the radiation detectors face the X-rays so that the detected X-ray signal is strongest," and thus does not fall within the protection scope of claim 1. According to the recording in claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, the only interpretation of "installation support" is the support for the radiation detectors, and claim 1 provides a functional limitation for this, i.e., "adjustable to ensure that the detection surfaces of the radiation detectors face the X-rays so that the detected X-ray signal is strongest." However, in the accused infringing product, the detectors on the transverse detection arm are directly fixed to the transverse detection arm, and there is no installation support on these detectors that can be adjusted to ensure that the detection surfaces face the X-rays for the strongest signal. Therefore, the accused infringing product does not possess the technical feature of the installation support as claimed in the patent-in-suit.

(d) Based on the above, the technical solution of the accused infringing product also does not fall within the protection scope of claims 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the patent-in-suit.

Third, the first-instance judgment equated the protection of the patented product with that of the accused infringing product, constituting an error in legal application. The accused infringing product in this case is the CBS62-405 container/vehicle inspection system. All claims of the patent-in-suit seek to protect "an arm structure of a double-view scanning apparatus." The arm structure is a component of the inspection system. The product claimed in the patent-in-suit (arm structure) cannot be equated with the inspection system product. Therefore, it cannot be determined that the inspection system product infringes the patent. The first-instance court erred in applying the law.

Fourth, the appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company did not engage in acts of offer for sale. The appellees Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company have no evidence to prove that Xuchang Ruishi Company committed acts of offer for sale.

Fifth, the first-instance judgment ordering the appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company to compensate the appellees Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company RMB 500,000 lacks factual and legal basis. The double-view scanning apparatus arm structure protected by all claims of the patent-in-suit is a component of the accused infringing product, CBS62-405 container/vehicle inspection system. It is a steel structural part with low finished product value. The lawyer fee invoices provided by Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company are not related to this case and cannot be proven to have been incurred for this case. The reasonable expenses for investigation and stopping the infringement also lack evidentiary support. Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company have not suffered losses, and Xuchang Ruishi Company has not gained profits. Therefore, the RMB 500,000 compensation lacks factual and legal basis. Request to set aside the first-instance judgment and either modify the judgment or remand for retrial.

The appellees Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company argued in defense: First, Tsinghua University, as a litigation subject in this case, complies with the provisions of Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and is a subject with a direct interest in this case. Nuctech Company originated from Tsinghua University, and the two cooperate closely. Moreover, the "Intellectual Property License and Use Certificate" clearly states that Tsinghua University has the right to assert claims against any infringing party together with Nuctech Company. Additionally, the law does not stipulate that non-profit institutions cannot file lawsuits. Tsinghua University is a proper plaintiff, and the first-instance court correctly applied the law. Second, the accused infringing product falls within the protection scope of claims 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the patent-in-suit. The first-instance judgment had clear fact findings and correct legal application. The accused infringing product falls within the protection scope of claim 1. There are only three differences between the two, and these differences constitute identical or equivalent technical features with the corresponding technical features in the patent-in-suit. Regarding the issue of the collimator column: the collimator column in the claim of the patent-in-suit has a collimator disposed therein, and the collimator column connects to the main beam above. The accelerator chamber and its upper support in the accused infringing product together constitute a support body, connected to the main beam, with a collimator disposed inside and also providing support for the collimator. The collimator column is not limited in shape or position. The two use substantially the same means, achieve substantially the same functions and effects, and a person of ordinary skill in the art, at the time of the alleged infringement, could conceive of this feature without creative effort. Thus, they constitute equivalent technical features. Regarding the uniform installation of radiation detectors: according to the claims and specification of the patent-in-suit, the uniform installation of the radiation detectors refers to the detectors being closely arranged within the two angled ray surface areas where X-rays are emitted, with the purpose of not missing any rays. It does not mean that the horizontal spacing of each detector on the transverse detection arm is equal. Based on the first-instance on-site inspection and preserved evidence, the detectors in the accused infringing product are arranged in the same manner. Regarding the adjustability of the installation support: according to the claims and specification of the patent-in-suit, the "transverse detection arm and installation support" in the patent-in-suit is the "installation support" for the radiation detectors, and the installation support is adjustable. Based on the first-instance inspection and preserved evidence, the transverse detection arm of the accused infringing product achieves the function of "adjusting the installation support" as required in claim 1 by changing the position of bolts in a cross-shaped installation slot, thereby ensuring that the detection surfaces of the radiation detectors face the X-rays. In summary, with respect to claim 1, the three points of contention raised by the appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company are all untenable. The accused infringing product falls within the protection scope of independent claim 1. The accused infringing product also falls within the protection scope of dependent claims 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8. Third, Xuchang Ruishi Company, without permission, committed patent infringement by offering for sale, including: (1) Xuchang Ruishi Company participated in customs bidding projects using the accused infringing product, thereby committing an act of offer for sale on its own; (2) Xuchang Ruishi Company and its parent company Shanghai Ruishi Company jointly committed acts of offer for sale. The first-instance inspection and preserved evidence showed the model of Xuchang Ruishi Company's infringing product and the fact that the machine bore the trademark of its parent company, Shanghai Ruishi Company. Additionally, evidence items 5 and 8 from the first instance demonstrated that Xuchang Ruishi Company and its parent company Shanghai Ruishi Company engaged in commercial advertising, exhibitions, and other acts of offer for sale for this model of infringing product. Fourth, the patent technology is advanced, and the patented product has a very high market share domestically and internationally, with high commercial value. The patent value cannot be assessed based on the value of raw materials. Moreover, the patent-in-suit is one of Nuctech Company's core patents. Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company incurred significant costs in investigating and stopping the infringement in this case. The damages awarded in the first-instance judgment are clearly too low. Request to dismiss the appeal and uphold the first-instance judgment.

During the second-instance trial by the Henan High People's Court, the appellees Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company jointly submitted two sets of new evidence:

First set of evidence: Notice of Composition of Collegial Panel for Administrative Case (2017) Jing 01 Xing Chu No. 1203 from the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court, the evidentiary catalog submitted by the Ministry of Finance of the People's Republic of China in that case, and item 6 of the defense materials in that catalog. This evidence originates from the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court and the Ministry of Finance. Purpose of proof: To prove that the appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company committed patent infringement, including the manufacture and offer for sale of the accused infringing product. In the case (2017) Jing 01 Xing Chu No. 1203 being heard by the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court, the court forwarded to Nuctech Company the evidentiary catalog and defense materials submitted by the Ministry of Finance on September 28, 2017, among which item 6 of the defense materials was issued by the Materials and Equipment Procurement Center of the General Administration of Customs at the request of the Ministry of Finance. Item 6 of the defense materials proves that Xuchang Ruishi Company bid for combined mobile inspection systems (Package 1), multifunctional large container/vehicle inspection systems (Package 2), and through-type rapid inspection systems (Package 5) to the Customs.

Second set of evidence: Invoices for reasonable expenses and service agreements. This evidence originates from the appellee Nuctech Company. Purpose of proof: To show that the damages awarded in the first-instance judgment are too low. This evidence includes two parts: (1) Agency/law service agreements respectively signed between Beijing Xingdi Law Firm and Beijing Huanqiu Law Firm with Nuctech Company regarding "infringement litigation" and "evidence preservation"; (2) Invoices for Nuctech Company's reasonable expenses, including: RMB 100,000 as basic attorney fees paid to Beijing Xingdi Law Firm; RMB 150,000 as first-instance success fees paid to Beijing Xingdi Law Firm; RMB 200,000 as first-instance success fees paid to Beijing Huanqiu Law Firm; RMB 450,000 as attorney fees for evidence preservation paid to Beijing Huanqiu Law Firm.

The appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company's opinions on the authentication of the above evidence: No objection to the authenticity of the above evidence, but objection to its relevance. The first set of evidence already existed at the first instance and should not be submitted as new evidence. The second set of evidence also already existed at the first instance and should not be submitted as new evidence. The above evidence should not be admitted.

Since the parties had no objection to the authenticity of the above evidence, the Henan High People's Court admitted it.

The Henan High People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

Additionally, it was found that: The appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Shanghai Ruishi Company, with the same legal representative.

The Henan High People's Court held in the second instance:

The issues in dispute in the second instance of this case are: 1. Whether the appellee Tsinghua University is a proper litigation subject; 2. Whether the accused infringing product falls within the protection scope of the patent claims; 3. Whether the appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company engaged in acts of offer for sale; 4. Whether the amount of damages in the first instance is appropriate.

1. Regarding whether the appellee Tsinghua University is a proper litigation subject. In this case, although the patentee of the patent-in-suit is the appellee Nuctech Company, the "Intellectual Property License and Use Certificate" issued by Nuctech Company explicitly authorizes Tsinghua University to use the patent-in-suit and to jointly assert rights with Nuctech Company against suspected infringers. Pursuant to Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China: "A lawsuit must meet the following conditions: (1) The plaintiff is a citizen, legal person, or other organization that has a direct interest in the case." Tsinghua University is a proper subject as a co-plaintiff in this case and may initiate relevant civil litigation. The first-instance court correctly applied the law, and it is affirmed. The appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company's ground of appeal that Tsinghua University is not a proper litigation subject is untenable and is dismissed.

2. Regarding whether the accused infringing product falls within the protection scope of the patent claims. In combination with the appeal, defense, and court trial, the dispute between the parties on this issue mainly focuses on three aspects of claim 1: (a) Whether the accelerator chamber and its upper support in the accused infringing product constitute equivalent technical features with the collimator column in the patent-in-suit; (b) Whether the detectors in the accused infringing product are uniformly installed; (c) Whether the installation support is adjustable.

(1) Regarding whether the accelerator chamber and its upper support bracket of the accused infringing product constitute equivalent technical features to the collimator column in the patent at issue. Article 59, paragraph 1, of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The scope of protection of the invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of the claims. The description and the drawings may be used to interpret the content of the claims." Article 17 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases provides: "The 'scope of protection of the invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of the claims, and the description and the drawings may be used to interpret the content of the claims' referred to in Article 59, paragraph 1, of the Patent Law means that the scope of protection of the patent right shall be determined by the scope determined by all the technical features recorded in the claims, and also includes the scope determined by features equivalent to such technical features. Equivalent features refer to features that, compared with the recorded technical features, achieve substantially the same function in substantially the same way to achieve substantially the same effect, and that can be conceived by a person of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the alleged infringing act without the need for creative labor." In this case, claim 1 of the patent at issue defines "the collimator column and the vertical detection arm are connected to the main beam, forming a frame, to provide support and adjustment mechanism for the collimator," but does not limit the specific structure of the collimator column. Based on the content of the claims, the function of the collimator column is to form part of the frame and to provide support for the collimator. Through on-site inspection, the accused infringing product does not have a component called a "collimator column." The accelerator chamber, its upper support bracket, the main beam, and the vertical detection arm of the accused infringing product form an integrally connected overall structure, jointly constituting a frame structure. The overall structure composed of the accelerator chamber and its upper support bracket in the accused infringing product also internally houses the collimator. Among them, the structure formed by the accelerator chamber together with its upper support bracket has the function of connecting with the main beam, forming part of the frame, and also has the function of supporting the collimator; both are substantially the same. From the analysis of function and effect, the collimator column, as part of the frame, provides support for the collimator. The accelerator chamber together with its upper support bracket in the accused infringing product constitutes a support body, the upper part of which is connected to the main beam, also as part of the overall frame, providing support for the collimator. Regardless of which structure is adopted, the functions and effects of both are substantially the same. Furthermore, a person of ordinary skill in the art could conceive of this type of support structure without the need for creative labor. Therefore, this support structure of the accused infringing product can be recognized as having the equivalent feature of the collimator column in the patent at issue. The appeal ground raised by Xuchang Ruishi Company that this support structure of the accused infringing product cannot be recognized as an equivalent feature of the collimator column in the patent at issue cannot be established and is dismissed.

(2) Regarding whether the detectors of the accused infringing product are evenly installed. Claim 1 of the patent at issue states: "on the horizontal detection arm, within the two angular radiation surface areas where X-rays are emitted, radiation detectors are evenly installed." Based on the working principle of the radiation detector and in conjunction with the patent specification, it is clear that the placement of the radiation detectors should be such that they can receive all radiation within the two angular radiation surface areas where X-rays are emitted. Correspondingly, the installation positions of the radiation detectors need to be scientifically calculated and reasonably designed based on different angles to ensure that no radiation is missed, thereby meeting the basic requirements for security inspection. Understanding the description of the technical feature of evenly installing detectors in claim 1, "evenly" does not mean that the horizontal spacing between individual detectors on the horizontal detection arm is equal. When the radiation emission area is determined, the installation positions of the radiation detectors are also fixed. Through on-site inspection, the installation mechanism of the radiation detectors in the accused infringing product is also to receive all radiation within the two angular radiation surface areas where X-rays are emitted. The installation positions of the radiation detectors are not randomly arranged but are reasonably determined through calculation based on different angles, achieving the technical effect of not missing any radiation. That is, the installation mechanism of the radiation detectors in the accused infringing product is the same as that in the patent at issue, and the installation method is the same as the technical feature of the patent at issue.

(3) Regarding whether the mounting bracket of the accused infringing product is adjustable. Claim 1 of the patent at issue states: "the mounting bracket for the radiation detectors can be adjusted to ensure that the detection surfaces of the radiation detectors face the X-rays directly, so that the detected X-ray signal is strongest," and based on the patent specification and drawings, it is known that the several radiation detectors in the patent are arranged in an array on the horizontal detection arm and the vertical detection arm. By adjusting the horizontal adjustment bolts, the horizontal detection arm can be translated and swung; by adjusting the vertical adjustment bolts, the relative position of the horizontal detection arm and the vertical detection arm can be adjusted. Adjusting the horizontal detection arm can adjust the array of radiation detectors to ensure that the detection surfaces of the radiation detectors face the X-rays directly, making the detected X-ray signal strongest. Through on-site inspection, the multiple radiation detectors in the accused infringing product are arranged in an array on the horizontal detection arm and the vertical detection arm. The horizontal detection arm can be adjusted in position by moving within two intersecting elongated mounting slots, thereby adjusting the multiple radiation detectors as a whole to ensure that the detection surfaces of the radiation detectors face the X-rays directly, making the detected X-ray signal strongest. That is, both can adjust the radiation detectors as a whole by adjusting the horizontal detection arm, and the technical feature is the same.

In summary, all technical features of the accused infringing product and claim 1 of the patent at issue are identical or equivalent, and thus the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of claim 1 of the patent at issue. The first instance judgment correctly found this and is affirmed.

Regarding claims 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8. The overall structure of the accused infringing product is a gantry structure, falling within the scope of protection of claim 2 of the patent at issue. Similar to the horizontal detection arm, the detectors on the vertical detection arm of the accused infringing product are evenly distributed within the radiation surface range, and there is an adjustment device that can adjust the position of the vertical detection arm to ensure that the detection surfaces of the radiation detectors face the X-rays directly, making the detected X-ray signal strongest. Therefore, it falls within the scope of protection of claim 4. The uppermost end of the radiation detectors on the vertical detection arm of the accused infringing product is higher than the radiation detectors installed on the horizontal detection arm, allowing detection of radiation on the diagonal of the detection surface. The accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of dependent claim 5 of the patent at issue. The collimator of the accused infringing product is connected to the collimator column via a lower support and an adjustment support, and can be translated and rotated through adjustment bolts, falling within the scope of protection of dependent claim 6 of the patent at issue. The horizontal detection arm of the accused infringing product is connected to the main beam via a mounting support, falling within the scope of protection of dependent claim 7 of the patent at issue. The adjustment device for the horizontal detection arm of the accused infringing product includes adjustment bolts, and achieves movement of the horizontal detection arm through displacement in the horizontal and vertical mounting slots, falling within the scope of protection of dependent claim 8 of the patent at issue.

In summary, the CBS62-405 container/vehicle inspection system manufactured by the appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company falls within the scope of protection of claims 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the invention patent No. ZL200710304704.8 entitled "Arm Structure of a Dual-View Scanning Device" owned by the appellees Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company, constituting patent infringement. The structure used on the accused infringing product is substantially the same in structure, purpose, and function as that of the patented product, and constitutes a main part of the accused infringing product. Xuchang Ruishi Company's arguments that it does not constitute infringement and that the arm structure is a component of the inspection system, therefore infringement of the arm structure cannot be deemed as infringement of the inspection system, cannot be established and are dismissed.

III. Regarding whether the appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company engaged in acts of offering for sale. Evidence from the on-site inspection at first instance shows that Xuchang Ruishi Company manufactured at least one set of CBS62-405 container/vehicle inspection system products, and this CBS62-405 product fully falls within the scope of protection of the patent at issue. The "Environmental Impact Report for the Production, Sales, and Use Project of Container Vehicle Inspection Equipment of Xuchang Ruishi Company" published on the Henan Provincial Environmental Protection Department website can prove that Xuchang Ruishi Company carried out relevant administrative approval procedures for the production of the accused infringing product. Combined with the evidence submitted by the appellees Nuctech Company and Tsinghua University at second instance, such as the certification issued by the Material and Equipment Procurement Center of the General Administration of Customs at the request of the Ministry of Finance of the People's Republic of China regarding the equipment combination bid by Xuchang Ruishi Company to the customs, it can be determined that Xuchang Ruishi Company's acts constitute manufacturing for the purpose of production and operation. Xuchang Ruishi Company, without permission, manufactured the patented product for the purpose of production and operation, constituting infringement, and shall bear the legal liabilities of ceasing infringement and compensating for losses. Additionally, based on the facts found at first instance, Shanghai Ruishi Company displayed similar products. As Xuchang Ruishi Company is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Shanghai Ruishi Company with the same legal representative, and the model, relevant function introduction, technical specifications, etc., of the product displayed by Shanghai Ruishi Company are consistent with the accused infringing product manufactured by Xuchang Ruishi Company, yet Xuchang Ruishi Company did not provide evidence showing that Shanghai Ruishi Company has other capabilities or premises for producing the displayed product, it can be determined that Xuchang Ruishi Company engaged in acts of offering for sale the accused infringing product. Xuchang Ruishi Company's appeal ground that it did not engage in acts of offering for sale cannot be established and is dismissed.

IV. Regarding whether the amount of compensation at first instance was appropriate. Pursuant to Article 65 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China: "The amount of compensation for patent infringement shall be determined based on the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to the infringement. If the actual losses are difficult to determine, the amount may be determined based on the benefits gained by the infringer from the infringement. If the losses of the right holder or the benefits gained by the infringer are difficult to determine, the amount may be reasonably determined by reference to the multiple of the patent license fee. The amount of compensation shall also include the reasonable expenses incurred by the right holder to stop the infringement. If the losses of the right holder, the benefits gained by the infringer, and the patent license fee are all difficult to determine, the people's court may, based on factors such as the type of the patent, the nature and circumstances of the infringement, determine an amount of compensation between RMB 10,000 and RMB 1,000,000." In this case, the appellees Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company did not submit sufficient evidence to prove the actual losses suffered due to the infringement or the benefits gained by the appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company from the infringement. The first instance court comprehensively considered that the patent at issue is an invention patent, the value of this type of complete equipment is relatively high, Nuctech Company's market share, Xuchang Ruishi Company is a manufacturing enterprise, and the reasonable expenses incurred by Tsinghua University and Nuctech Company for investigation and stopping the infringement in this case, and determined the compensation amount of RMB 500,000 by discretion, which is not improper and is affirmed. Xuchang Ruishi Company's appeal ground on this issue cannot be established and is dismissed.

In conclusion, the appeal requests of the appellant Xuchang Ruishi Company cannot be established and should be dismissed; the first instance judgment correctly found the facts and applied the law, and should be affirmed. The Henan High People's Court, pursuant to Item (1) of Article 170, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, hereby rules on September 30, 2018, as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
